Mondays are an optional session/office hour. The first half of the semester, those Mondays are **Base Camp**: particularly useful if you are new to all of this, but open to everyone. No attendance is taken, nothing here affects your grade in any direction, but you will have a better grasp of the material at the end of each session. Plus, it's a good way to meet some more people in the class and to talk to me/the TA!

::: {.column-margin}
The second half of the semester, Mondays become [Side Quests](sidequests.qmd) — interesting extensions beyond the core course content.
:::


<!-- **Base Camp is not remedial.** Maybe haven't done this before and it didn't click the first time, or maybe you just want the extra practice, or maybe you just want to meet some more people in the class.  -->
<!-- Plenty of your classmates arrive with years of tinkering; you're not behind them in ability, you're behind them in *hours*, and hours are exactly what Mondays supply. The course was designed assuming zero prior experience. Base Camp is where that assumption gets honored with an instructor at your elbow. -->


*Time and room set by signup poll in week 1 — watch Canvas.*

## The sessions

**BC1 (Week 1) · The computer itself, and how to talk about code.** Before any coding: the computer itself. Browsers vs. apps, Colab login, where a downloaded file goes, folders, uploading to Colab, what "the cloud" means for your work. Then the second half: **how to ask a question about code** — the vocabulary (what do you call `**`, `[]`, `:`?), the best way to ask a question: *what I ran / what I expected / what I got instead*. 
<!-- How you'd ask a TA, how you'd ask your table, and how you'd prompt an LLM. -->

**BC2 (Week 2) · First contact, slowly.** The [week 2 lesson](../lessons/02a-first-contact.qmd) again at half speed: cells, variables, running your first program, and learning to read error messages as information instead of accusation.

**BC3 (Week 3) · The vocabulary drill.** Reps on the core reading skills: trace variables by hand, predict outputs, read `=` as "is assigned." Includes **assembly problems** — working code with its lines scrambled.

**BC4 (Week 4) · Dress rehearsal: Checkpoint 1.** A full practice checkpoint under real conditions — paper, timed, no AI — then we rework it together, item by item. **Dress rehearsals repeat on the Monday before every checkpoint** (weeks 4, 6, 8, 10).

**BC5 (Week 5) · Loop clinic.** Loops trip up more beginners than any other fundamental ingredient. Extra reps with accumulators, `range`, predicting iteration by hand, and loop assembly.

**BC6 (Week 6) · Dress rehearsal: Checkpoint 2** — including re-offer items from Checkpoint 1, just as Tuesday will.

## Practice library (async Base Camp)

I'll add extra code traces, predict-then-runs, and assembly problems, with collapsible answers. Requests welcome. Page is up: **[Practice Library](practice.qmd)**.
